memories.content: Attach adjacent evidence or citations to verifiable claims about user behavior or technology effects.
Distinguish between results observed in the pilot and expectations to be confirmed in the main user study using different expressions.
Do not use verbs that imply proving causation if the design does not support causal inference.
For topics with sufficient HCI research evidence, prioritize citing recent comprehensive studies over listing individual cases.
Explain how each design choice was derived to address specific user needs.
Support each core claim with evidence that directly examined it rather than with indirect summaries.
Reviewers first check the direct evidence placed closest to the core claim.
Connect the proposed conceptual design principle to at least one observable user behavior.
Identify which design judgment—retain, modify, or discard—each piece of evidence from formative evaluation supports.
Results from controlled formative studies do not directly prove effects in actual long-term use.
The user can have an explanation approved as a conceptual contribution only if it is falsifiable with observable data.
Calculate user research compensation budgets based on the estimated participation burden, combining session time with required technical and travel preparation.
Compensate participants who withdraw from the study midway for their actual participation time.
Compensate for the time actually spent in sessions, regardless of the research modality.
Allow the issuance of gift cards of equivalent value to participants in remote studies who cannot use electronic transfers.
Do not treat an unresolved payment method as a deficiency at the proposal stage.
Allow differential compensation amounts for on-site and remote studies when participation burden varies due to travel or technical preparation.
Participants judge the fairness of compensation based on the combined burden of session time and required technical and travel preparation.
In longitudinal studies requiring diary entries and repeated reporting, include out-of-session recording time in compensation calculations.
Distinguish between participant research compensation and labor costs for field staff performing installation and operational support as part of their duties.
The user tends to count session time but omit participants’ advance setup and follow-up reporting time.

analysis.overview: The frames address separate operational domains. The reference frame governs evidence, causal language, design rationale, and conceptual contribution standards, while the compared frame governs participant compensation, burden accounting, payment methods, and distinctions from staff labor costs. Neither side supplies a scope-aligned counterpart to the other.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame defines burden-based participant compensation, including withdrawal, modality, preparation, travel, diary work, payment alternatives, proposal-stage flexibility, fairness perceptions, common budgeting omissions, and separation from field-staff labor costs.
reports.reference_only: The reference frame sets standards for claim support, evidence placement and quality, causal restraint, pilot-versus-main-study wording, design traceability, formative-evaluation judgments, and observable, falsifiable conceptual contributions.
